ahead: This task is a completed, primarily negative investigation (which the assignment itself allows as a valid, complete result), not a proof. Two things remain open for whoever works Z_(q) next: (1) the literature citation in RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 2 (Montgomery-Vaughan, 'The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem,' Acta Arith. 27 (1975), 353-370, for the classical asymptotic sum_{n<=N} r(n)^2 ~ C N^3 where r(n)=sum_{n1+n2=n} Lambda(n1)Lambda(n2)) is stated from recollection, not verified against a live source -- this worktree has no network access or bibliographic database, only grep/rg/ls/cat/head/tail/wc/find and the lab's bare Python interpreter, so nobody in this environment can currently verify it independently; if a future attempt gets literature-search access, checking that citation (and searching further for an arc-restricted, (q,a)-indexed analogue of Montgomery-Vaughan's log-power-saving mean-square-exceptional-set result, which this document explicitly does not find) is the natural next step. (2) The irreducible core this document isolates, integral_{I_{q,a}} |F_N|^4 dalpha (a raw, unweighted, unrestricted local fourth moment of the prime exponential sum on a single arc of width ~1/(qN) around a/q, for q up to R_0 ~ sqrt(N)/(3 log N)), is not bounded here and is, as far as this document's search went, not bounded by any tool named in UPPER_BOUND.md, RANK3_SCOPE.md, or found in this document's literature search; a genuinely new, unconditional bound on exactly that quantity at q lesssim N^{2/5} is what would be needed, and this document gives the reasons (section 1's three failed transfer mechanisms, section 2's Theta(N^3) full-circle floor) why the obvious approaches do not supply one.

work.what: Verify, using literature-search tooling not available in worktree a-0044, whether Montgomery and Vaughan's paper 'The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem,' Acta Arithmetica 27 (1975), pp. 353-370, actually contains the claimed asymptotic sum_{n<=N} r(n)^2 ~ C*N^3 (with r(n) = sum_{n1+n2=n, 1<=n1,n2<=N} Lambda(n1)*Lambda(n2), Lambda the von Mangoldt function, and C an explicit constant from the singular series average) as a two-sided (not just upper-bound) unconditional asymptotic, and whether it also contains sum_{n<=N} (r(n) - S(n)*n)^2 << N^3*(log N)^{-A} for every fixed A>0 (S(n) the pointwise-in-n singular series). Report exact theorem numbers/statements if found, or that the paper does not contain this content if it does not, or point to the correct reference if the content exists but is misattributed. Context: hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 2 in the prime_pair_error hunt of this repository relies on this citation (from an agent's training-data recollection, not verified against a live source) to argue that the full-circle quartic moment integral_0^1 |F_N(alpha)|^4 dalpha (F_N(alpha) = sum_{n<=N} Lambda(n) e(n*alpha)) is provably Theta(N^3), which is used to explain why no fourth-moment tool can supply a power-saving for that full-circle quantity, sharpening an existing 'no tool found' wall into a proved obstruction. If the citation is wrong or the claimed content does not match, hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 2 needs correcting to whatever the literature actually supports (or a fresh negative finding if nothing of this shape is available unconditionally).

In the prime_pair_error hunt, hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 1 shows that every natural arc-transfer mechanism for the fourth residual moment Z_(q) (defined in hunts/prime_pair_error/UPPER_BOUND.md section 6 and hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_SCOPE.md section 1) reduces to bounding integral_{I_{q,a}} |F_N(alpha)|^4 dalpha directly, where F_N(alpha) = sum_{n<=N} Lambda(n) e(n*alpha) (Lambda = von Mangoldt function), I_{q,a} is the minor arc of width ~1/(qN) around the rational a/q (gcd(a,q)=1), for moduli q in the range 2 <= q <= R_0 = floor(sqrt(N)/3)/log(N), and specifically that this is hardest at q lesssim N^{2/5} where Vaughan's exponential sum bound gives no saving over the trivial |F_N| = O(N) (this sub-range is a strict subset of 2<=q<=R_0 since R_0 grows like N^{1/2}/log N, faster than N^{2/5}). Task: find or construct an unconditional bound on integral_{I_{q,a}} |F_N|^4 dalpha, summed over reduced residues a mod q and over 2<=q<=R_0, that beats the trivial order O(N^3) (per q, summed to more than O(N^3) overall) -- ideally reaching O(N^{2+epsilon}) total. hunts/prime_pair_error/RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 2 shows the full-circle (q=1, unrestricted) version of this same quantity is provably Theta(N^3) via the classical mean-square theory of Goldbach representations (subject to independent verification, see work item w-verify-mv-goldbach-citation), so any saving has to come specifically from the arc-restriction (width ~1/(qN) versus the full circle), not from the quartic moment itself being smaller than its known full-circle size. Do not weaken the definitions of Z_(q), R_0, F_N, or the reduced-residue/coprimality conditions.

edges.why: If the Montgomery-Vaughan citation is wrong or does not establish Theta(N^3) unconditionally for the full-circle quartic moment, the reasoning in RANK3_QUARTIC_LITERATURE.md section 2 that motivates looking specifically at the arc-restriction (rather than at the full-circle quartic moment itself) needs to be re-derived or reconsidered before work on the arc-restricted bound can trust that framing.
